title: Second Half 2026 Release: What’s New in SAP SuccessFactors HCM?
author: jeffreyglauber
text:
The SAP SuccessFactors 2H 2026 release marks an important milestone. It is the first major wave of innovation since SAP announced its vision for Autonomous HCM, where AI orchestrates end-to-end processes, drives context-aware decisions, and optimizes workforce operations at scale. In this release, we are delivering hundreds of new capabilities and enhancements across the suite that will bring this vision to life. 
 Here’s a snapshot of some of the key innovations, aligned to stages of the employee lifecycle: 

 Plan & Hire 

 Recruiting 
 Internal hires can now route automatically from SmartRecruiters for SAP SuccessFactors to SAP SuccessFactors Onboarding and SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central, with sync status visible in real time, keeping recruiting and core HR data aligned. Additionally, business rules now connect SmartRecruiters solutions data to configurable automation, removing manual steps across the hiring workflow. 
 Winston Match results are now fully reportable in Report Builder, including overall match bands and dimension-level detail across jobs and applications. Recruiters can see exactly how AI-driven candidate rankings affect pipeline progression, connect scoring to hiring outcomes, and review or explain AI-assisted decisions with confidence, making it easier to identify the candidates most likely to succeed. Winston Screen builds on this by applying repeatable, configurable screening questions consistently across roles, helping recruiters narrow large applicant pools more efficiently, with results reportable in Report Builder alongside the full pipeline. 
 Winston Screen 

 A new agentic scheduling capability, available through Winston Companion, enables interviews to be booked with a single prompt, replacing fragmented manual coordination. And during interviews, the new Interview Summary Agent automatically captures and posts a structured interview summary to the candidate profile. This agent works directly with Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, and Gong. 
 Agentic scheduling 

 Onboarding 
 The Onboarding Assistant helps HR teams deliver personalized new hire experiences at scale through agentic capabilities that provide intelligent prioritization, simplified task creation, and automated custom form conversion. The assistant delivers AI-orchestrated task tracking that coordinates and tracks onboarding actions, highlights clear next best steps, and surfaces bottlenecks or risks before they delay onboarding progress. To further support day-one readiness, HR teams can also use the assistant to easily create unique onboarding tasks and localized, custom multilingual forms. 
 Onboarding Assistant 

 Manage & Pay 

 Core HR 
 The HR Operations Assistant allows organizations to manage workforce data and employee changes more intelligently. The assistant proactively identifies and resolves data issues, streamlines employment and organizational changes, accelerates workflows, optimizes position management, and helps safeguard payroll-related transactions. AI agents continuously monitor employee, job, position, and payroll-related data for inconsistencies, surfacing issues with context and guided resolution before they impact downstream processes. 
 HR Operations Assistant 

 New organizational modeling capabilities in SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central provide HR teams and business leaders with a collaborative environment to create structured modeling projects, document business rationale, and manage stakeholder participation through role-based access. Multiple simulation versions allow teams to visualize structural changes using drag-and-drop interactions for targeted restructures or a list view for mass updates. Once the preferred scenario is finalized, a controlled cascading save automatically applies updates across every affected organizational object in SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central. 
 Organizational Modeling in SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central 

 A new agentic U.S. benefits administration console in SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Global Benefits gives administrators a unified view of benefits processes, helping them identify issues faster, streamline enrollment management, and improve productivity. 

 Payroll 
 The Payroll Assistant serves as an AI partner for both payroll administrators and employees, delivering guidance, insights, and support when it’s needed most. For payroll administrators, the assistant can answer complex questions, provide context-aware guidance, identify alerts, and take corrective action before alerts escalate into errors. It continuously monitors payroll data to proactively identify anomalies and compliance gaps, replacing reactive audits with real-time intelligence. Employees can interact directly with the assistant to understand their pay and resolve paycheck questions without raising a support ticket. 
 Payroll Assistant 

 Ukraine is now available as a native payroll country version in SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll, bringing native coverage to 54 countries, plus seven additional countries supported by partners. 

 Workforce management 
 Organizations can now leverage a consolidated timesheet experience across SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP SuccessFactors Time Tracking, transforming how time is managed across the project lifecycle. It gives consultants a single experience to record both project work and HR attendance, eliminating double entry. Work schedules, absences, and compliance rules sync automatically from SAP SuccessFactors solutions, while approved time flows directly into payroll and project billing without manual reconciliation. The result is a connected experience across every phase from resource planning through time capture to revenue recognition in one intelligent, integrated suite. 
 Consolidated timesheet 

 HR service delivery 
 The HR Service Assistant helps employees get answers and complete tasks across HR, payroll, time, and knowledge services. Employees receive cited, policy-grounded responses sourced from company documentation and external providers. The assistant guides employees through actions such as checking leave balances, submitting time-off requests, or receiving personalized answers to policy-related questions. 
 HR Service Assistant 

 For HR service teams, the Case Management Assistant brings AI-generated case summaries, contextual insights, and next-best-action recommendations directly into the SAP SuccessFactors Enterprise Service Management solution workflow. 
 A redesigned self-service landing page in SAP SuccessFactors Enterprise Service Management provides a single, intuitive destination where employees can search for help, track open cases, and check request status without switching tools or waiting for support. Additionally, a generative knowledge creation capability automatically drafts and refines knowledge base articles from closed cases, turning today’s solutions into tomorrow’s self-service answers. 

 Platform 
 Our suite-first strategy advances further with deeper SAP Task Center app integration for unified workflows and our SAP-managed integration between SAP SuccessFactors HCM and the SAP S/4HANA Finance solution. This removes the need for you to provision and maintain the integration yourself. And with new ISO 27701 (privacy information management) and ISO 42001 (AI management systems) certifications, we further strengthen our commitment to global compliance and responsible AI. 

 Develop & Grow 

 Performance and goals 
 The Performance & Goals Assistant creates strategically aligned goals and continuously monitors progress and business impact. It also supports managers in preparing for performance check-ins and reviews, helping drive fair, data-driven decisions. Real-time insights and bias detection enable more objective evaluations and support equitable rating discussions. By highlighting potential equity concerns throughout the calibration process, it helps organizations improve transparency, strengthen consistency, and build greater employee trust. 
 Performance & Goals Assistant 

 Career and talent development 
 The Career and Talent Development Assistant creates strategically aligned development plans and cultivates healthy talent pipelines. AI agents continuously monitor individual development needs and provide tailored career guidance, helping ensure talent readiness and engagement. 
 Career and Talent Development Assistant 

 The Skills Governance Agent (part of the HR Operations Assistant) continuously analyzes the skills library and recommends concrete actions for HR teams to keep the data current which means less manual work, stronger talent-to-opportunity matching, and more reliable skills reporting. Additionally, the Job Architecture Management Agent (also part of the HR Operations Assistant) monitors job architecture, comparing the skills roles require against what employees have, what recruiters are hiring for, and what’s in the job profiles, flagging where roles are outdated or missing. The result is a living job architecture, rather than a point-in-time document. 
 Skills Governance Agent 

 Certificates from the talent intelligence hub can now be linked to job roles within job profile builder. This enhances employee career path visibility, strengthens qualification tracking, and improves governance of role-based certification requirements. Additionally, customers can now import bulk certificate master data records and employee certificate portfolios, eliminating manual entry for high volumes of certificates. 

 Learning 
 The Learning Assistant equips organizations with improved compliance monitoring, assignment creation, learning journeys, and skills-based learning recommendations delivered in a more automated and personalized way. It helps guide the right learning actions at the right time for employees, managers, and admins. From monitoring compliance training deadlines and notifying learners and managers to identifying team skill gaps and recommending targeted learning, the assistant connects compliance, upskilling, and development in one experience. 
 Learning Assistant 

 WalkMe Learning Arc, an AI-native content creation solution, is now integrated with SAP SuccessFactors Learning. With WalkMe Learning Arc, admins and managers can take advantage of AI to generate structure and draft content, simulations, and self-checks, all while suggesting metadata and producing finished courses that publish back into SAP SuccessFactors Learning. 
 WalkMe Learning Arc integration with SAP SuccessFactors Learning 

 Learn more 
 These are just a few of the many innovations in the SAP SuccessFactors 2H 2026 release. To learn more, check out the resources below: 
 Visit the SAP SuccessFactors Product Release & Road Map Information page for release documentation, videos, and blogs. 
 Watch the 2H 2026 Release Highlights Overview Video , featuring Rebecca Carr, President of HCM Products at SAP

title: Delete the Training Pipeline
author: andreas_roth
text: Your lakehouse is fresh. Why are your forecasts still days old? Most predictive ML architectures contain the same contradiction: a continuously updated, zero-copy lakehouse feeds a pipeline that freezes the data, trains one model per tenant and use case, and retrains it on a schedule. Three thousand tenants and four use cases already mean twelve thousand model artifacts—each with its own lifecycle and its own shadow copy of data you spent a decade centralizing. Tabular foundation models offer a radically different architecture. They can predict from labeled rows supplied as context at request time: no per-tenant training run, no model artifact, no frozen extract. One shared, stateless model can replace the **N × M × R** multiplication of tenants, use cases, and retrains. What happens when you delete the training pipeline? Tenant onboarding becomes a query scope. The feature store loses its reason to exist. The federated Iceberg lakehouse becomes the serving layer—and model freshness collapses into data freshness. The architectural fit is unusually exact: tabular foundation models need live, governed, point-in-time addressable data; the modern lakehouse was built to provide precisely that. But the work does not disappear. It moves into context selection, governance, point-in-time reproducibility, and inference latency. This article traces that architectural shift and tests it through three experiments using TabPFN, Dremio, and Iceberg: comparing shared and per-tenant model accuracy, preserving isolation across physically separate tables, and reproducing past predictions from lakehouse snapshots.

title: SAP TM Clean Core extensibility, API-first integration, and intelligent logistics automation
author: Rogerio_Lima1
text:
Introduction 
 Follow my previous blog SAP Transportation Management Clean Core Evolution - SAP Community. As part of the continuous evolution of SAP TM SAP S/4HANA marks a pivotal milestone for SAP Transportation Management (TM). This release delivers a cohesive set of innovations that collectively advance three strategic imperatives: Clean Core extensibility, API-first integration, and intelligent logistics automation. The 49 SAP Notes documented in this blog represent the authoritative reference for architects, developers, and functional consultants who need to understand what has changed, why it matters, and how to act on it. 
 The notes are organised into eight thematic areas — each with a curated list of notes and an architectural commentary that frames the changes within the broader SAP Logistics landscape. A full reference table at the end provides a one-page summary of all 49 notes. 
 1 CDS Views & Virtual Data Model (VDM) 
 The Virtual Data Model is the foundation of SAP's Clean Core strategy. C1-released CDS view entities provide stable, versioned interfaces that partners and customers can consume without risk of breaking changes at upgrade. S/4HANA 2025 introduces new VDM artefacts for the Transportation Order model and for the Material and Location business objects. 
 SAP Note 3840080 New V2 view I_MaterialFreightGroup_2 (C1 released) 
 SAP Note 3838137 VDM Foundation layer for TOR Party node 
 SAP Note 3780776 TM: Enable enhancement of BO Material root via CDS view entity 
 SAP Note 3756405 TM: Enable enhancement of BO Location root via CDS view entity 
 Architectural Commentary 
 SAP Note 3840080 elevates I_MaterialFreightGroup to a V2-stable, C1-released interface, making it safe to consume in BTP extension projects, fiori apps, and analytical queries without worrying about undocumented changes at upgrade time. SAP Note 3838137 delivers the VDM foundation for the Party node of the Transportation Order — a prerequisite for downstream data product and API capabilities introduced elsewhere in this release. 

 Notes 3780776 and 3756405 are architecturally significant: they expose the Material and Location business object roots as CDS view entities, enabling BAdI-based enhancement in a fully Clean Core-compliant way. This replaces the need for implicit enhancements or custom dictionary includes, and aligns with the SAP BTP extensibility model where side-by-side extensions interact with the core through stable, released interfaces. 
 2 Location & Organisational Units Data Products 
 Data Products represent SAP's next-generation approach to master data consumption: semantically annotated, OData-ready, and governed through a formal release contract. S/4HANA 2025 completes the Location and Organisational Unit data product foundation for SAP TM, delivering the full stack from core CDS views through data provider infrastructure to service exposure. 
 SAP Note 3677186 S/4HANA 2025 Development – TM Clean Core Location CDS view foundation 
 SAP Note 3696891 S/4HANA 2025 Development – Location core CDS views, Data Product and Data Provider views 
 SAP Note 3747480 S/4HANA 2025 Development – Location Data Product – boolean annotations 
 SAP Note 3727007 S/4HANA 2025 Development – Service Development for Location and Org Units Data Products 
 Architectural Commentary 
 The four notes in this group follow a deliberate layering pattern. SAP Note 3677186 creates the stable CDS-view foundation for Location master data — the single source of truth. Note 3696891 builds the data product and data provider views on top, while Note 3747480 corrects boolean annotation semantics that affect downstream OData filter and search behaviour. Note 3727007 completes the picture by exposing Location and Org Units through OData services. 

 The Org Units data product in Note 3727007 is particularly valuable for organisations integrating SAP TM with SAP S/4HANA Central Finance or SAP Analytics Cloud, as it provides a standardised, API-accessible interface to the organisational hierarchy without custom BAPI wrappers. 
 3 Transportation Order (TOR) & Clean Core Extensions 
 The Transportation Order is the central business object in SAP TM, orchestrating the full freight lifecycle from order entry through carrier assignment to proof of delivery. S/4HANA 2025 delivers a wave of Clean Core enhancements — new data products, remote APIs, and creation types — that deepen the TOR model while preserving a clean, stable core. 
 SAP Note 3803774 BDC/Data Product – TOR (S/4HANA 2025) 
 SAP Note 3688875 BDC/Data Product – TOR (S/4HANA 2025) 
 SAP Note 3675348 Clean Core TOR TP Enhancement & Remote API 
 SAP Note 3691780 Clean Core TOR Foundation Enhancement 
 SAP Note 3791310 New TOR Creation Type for Local API 
 Architectural Commentary 
 Notes 3803774 and 3688875 deliver the Business Document Composition (BDC) data product for the TOR, enabling standardised document exchange in SAP Business Network for Logistics scenarios and providing a governed read interface for the full TOR payload. 
 Note 3691780 provides the Clean Core foundation that every subsequent TOR extension builds on — without it, custom fields and logic added via BTP extension projects cannot attach cleanly to the TOR. Note 3675348 introduces Remote API capabilities for Transportation Planning enhancements, allowing side-by-side BTP extensions to interact with TOR planning logic on the S/4HANA backend. Note 3791310 adds a dedicated TOR creation type for local API-driven scenarios, relevant for event-driven architectures and integration via SAP Integration Suite. 
 4 Order Management — Advance Developments 
 S/4HANA 2025 introduces a significant cluster of advance developments in Order Management, delivered through a coordinated set of SAP Notes. These notes extend Freight Order and Transportation Order capabilities with new fields, UI improvements, and process logic — collectively raising the bar for end-to-end order lifecycle management in SAP TM. 
 SAP Note 3841367 Advance Developments for S/4HANA TM – Order Management 
 SAP Note 3841186 Advance Developments for S/4HANA TM – Order Management 
 SAP Note 3840156 Advance Development in the Area of Order Management 
 SAP Note 3839471 Advance Developments for S/4HANA TM – Order Management 
 SAP Note 3837052 Advance Development in the Area of Order Management 
 SAP Note 3839570 Advance Developments for S/4HANA TM – Order Management 
 SAP Note 3805411 Enhancements in freight order management 
 SAP Note 3418826 TM: Cumulative enhancements (S/4HANA 2025) 
 Architectural Commentary 
 The volume of Order Management notes in S/4HANA 2025 reflects the strategic importance of this domain. Notes 3841367, 3841186, 3840156, 3839471, 3837052, and 3839570 form a coordinated advance development package — each addressing a specific aspect of order lifecycle management such as status handling, document flow, and carrier integration. These notes should be applied as a set; partial application may leave the system in an inconsistent state. 

 Note 3805411 targets Freight Order management specifically, adding UI fields and processing logic that support the expanded order scenarios introduced in this release. Note 3418826 is the cumulative enhancement note — it consolidates corrections and incremental improvements and should be a standard part of any S/4HANA 2025 maintenance patching checklist. 

 Recommendation: Review all Order Management advance development notes (3841367, 3841186, 3840156, 3839471, 3837052, 3839570) together with your SAP TM functional lead before applying. Regression testing on Freight Order creation, status transitions, and carrier assignment workflows is strongly advised. 
 5 Event Reporting & Trigger Handling 
 Real-time visibility and event-driven processing are critical capabilities for modern logistics networks. S/4HANA 2025 advances both areas with dedicated developments for Event Reporting and Trigger Handling within SAP TM. 
 SAP Note 3840749 Advance Developments for S/4HANA TM – Event Reporting 
 SAP Note 3839577 Advance Development for S/4HANA TM – Trigger Handling 
 Architectural Commentary 
 SAP Note 3840749 extends the Event Reporting framework within SAP TM — enabling richer, more granular shipment event capture and reporting. For organisations running SAP Track and Trace or integrating with SAP Business Network for Logistics, this note is a key enabler of real-time visibility dashboards and exception-based alerting. 

 SAP Note 3839577 targets Trigger Handling — the mechanism by which SAP TM reacts to upstream events (e.g. goods issue, delivery creation, EWM transfer order confirmation) and initiates downstream TM processes automatically. title: SAP CPQ : The Future of Sales Quoting Is Here: Meet SAP's Joule Quoting Assistant
author: Yogananda
text:
How AI is transforming one of sales' most time-consuming processes 
 Every sales rep knows the pain. A customer sends over an email — or a ten-page PDF — and suddenly you're spending the better part of your afternoon manually parsing the request, matching products, checking pricing rules, and assembling a proposal document. It's repetitive, error-prone, and it gets in the way of actual selling. 

 SAP's Joule Quoting Assistant is designed to change that entirely. 
 What Is the Joule Quoting Assistant? 
 The Joule Quoting Assistant is an AI-powered Joule Assistant — part of SAP's broader agentic AI portfolio — built specifically for the quote-to-order cycle. Its core mission: transform unstructured customer requests into accurate, compliant quotes with AI-guided selling across the entire SAP CPQ (Configure, Price, Quote) flow. Source 
 It sits at the intersection of SAP CPQ, SAP Sales Cloud, and SAP S/4HANA, orchestrating specialized AI agents behind the scenes to handle tasks that would otherwise fall to the sales rep or a back-office support team. 
 From Inbox to Quote: What It Actually Does 
 Here's where the Quoting Assistant gets practical. Given an unstructured customer inquiry — whether it arrives as an email, a request for quotation (RFQ), or a PDF — the assistant can: 
 Convert the raw request into a structured CPQ quote draft , extracting relevant intent and mapping it to your product catalog and pricing rules. 
 Recommend compliant product configurations based on what the customer described in natural language — no need to manually navigate complex configurators. 
 Surface real-time upsell, add-on, and cross-sell options guided by historical deal data and pricing policies. 
 Assemble proposal documents and draft customer-facing emails , ready for the rep to review and send. 
 Route multi-step requests to the right specialized agents automatically, without manual handoffs. 
 Enforce pricing and discount policies — every quote stays within guardrails, reducing approvals overhead and compliance risk. Source 
 Why This Matters for your Sales Teams 
 The shift from manual quoting to AI-guided quoting isn't just about speed — it changes the quality and consistency of the entire sales conversation. 
 Faster time to first draft. Instead of spending hours building a quote from scratch, reps get an intelligent draft that's already shaped by the customer's actual request. That frees them up to focus on relationship management and deal strategy. 
 Better accuracy and compliance. When pricing rules, discount limits, and configuration constraints are embedded in the assistant's reasoning, errors are caught before they reach the customer — not after an internal audit. 
 Higher deal size through guided selling. Real-time upsell and cross-sell recommendations aren't an afterthought; they're built into the quoting flow. Reps are prompted with relevant options at exactly the right moment. 
 Tighter SAP ecosystem integration. The Quoting Assistant works natively within SAP CPQ and SAP S/4HANA, which means no data re-entry, clean-core alignment, and full traceability across the quote lifecycle. Source 
 The Architecture Behind It: Assistants + Agents 
 The Quoting Assistant doesn't work alone. It's part of SAP's layered AI architecture: Joule Assistants — role-aligned, context-aware AI systems — sit above Joule Agents , which are the task specialists that execute individual steps. Source 
 You tell the Quoting Assistant what you want to accomplish in plain language. It interprets your intent, pulls in your business context (your CPQ rules, your pricing policies, your customer history), and coordinates the agents doing the actual work. You stay in control; the heavy lifting happens automatically. 
 This architecture is important because it means the Quoting Assistant isn't a standalone tool — it's part of SAP's Autonomous Enterprise vision, where AI handles routine execution so people can focus on decisions that require judgment. 
 A Real-World Scenario 
 Imagine a key account manager receives an email from a customer requesting a customised bundle of hardware and professional services across three countries, with specific delivery windows and a tight margin requirement. 
 Historically, this would take hours — coordinating with product management, pricing, and legal before a quote could even be drafted. 
 With the Joule Quoting Assistant, the rep pastes (or forwards) the customer email, and the assistant: 
 Parses the request and maps it to available products and service SKUs. 
 Checks configuration rules and flags any incompatible options. 
 Proposes a compliant price structure with margin guardrails. 
 Recommends a maintenance bundle and a support tier upsell. 
 Drafts the proposal document and a personalised cover email. 
 The rep reviews, adjusts, approves. What took half a day now takes minutes. 
 What This Signals for the Future of Sales 
 SAP's investment in the Quoting Assistant reflects a broader industry shift: the sales rep of the near future is a reviewer and relationship manager, not a data entry clerk . AI handles the structure; humans handle the nuance. 
 For organisations running SAP CPQ or SAP Sales Cloud v2, this isn't a distant roadmap item — it's available now, and it integrates with the systems you already have. The question isn't whether to evaluate it; it's how quickly you can get it into the hands of your team. 
 The SAP Joule Quoting Assistant is part of the SAP Joule Assistants portfolio. Learn more at sap.com/use-cases/joule-assistant/quoting-ai .

title: Track Your Private Cloud Journey: New Adoption Milestones powered by SAP EarlyWatch Alert
author: Michael_Hoppe
text:
We are excited to announce a new capability for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition customers: adoption milestone tracking, powered by SAP EarlyWatch Alert data and available in the Customer Insights Dashboard (CID) on SAP for Me. 
 If you are already familiar with the onboarding milestones for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP Integrated Business Planning (IBP), this is the Private Cloud counterpart you have been waiting for. And it goes even further: in addition to tracking implementation progress, the new milestones include built-in adoption risk monitoring that continuously watches for early signs of stalled implementations or declining system usage. 

 Why This Matters 
 Moving to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition is one of the most significant transformations a business can undertake. The journey from contract signature to a fully operational, value-generating system can span months, sometimes even years, of provisioning, configuration, testing and go-live activities. 
 Yet for much of that journey, the signals that indicate whether a customer is progressing as expected, or beginning to stall, have been difficult to surface systematically. Data was fragmented across tools, inputs were manual, and adoption risk was often identified too late for meaningful intervention. 
 The question we set out to answer: How can we generate data-driven insights on adoption journeys, early enough to make a real difference? 

 What SAP EarlyWatch Alert Brings to the Table 
 SAP EarlyWatch Alert has been a trusted companion for SAP customers for decades, indicating system health, performance, and configuration. With this new release, SAP EarlyWatch Alert further expands its scope beyond system diagnostics into adoption intelligence. Here is what makes this approach unique: 
 Zero configuration. SAP EarlyWatch Alert already collects weekly telemetry data from every connected system: active users, transport activity, transaction usage, and more. No additional setup is required from the customer. 
 Fully automated. Milestones are automatically recalculated twice per week across all connected S/4HANA Private Cloud landscapes. 
 Proactive risk detection. The dashboard does not just track forward progress. It also continuously monitors signs of stalled adoption and user decline after go-live. 
 Integrated experience. Milestone data appears in the Onboarding tab of the Customer Insights Dashboard in SAP for Me, right alongside Public Cloud and IBP milestones. 
 The SAP EarlyWatch Alert Apps as tools for proactive alerting and diagnostics can be accessed via SAP for Me: https://me.sap.com/servicessupport/diagnostics 

 The Six Adoption Milestones 
 Each SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition system landscape is tracked through six milestones that map to the key phases of a new cloud ERP implementation or transformation approach. Milestones are evaluated per system track, which is the logical grouping of a customer's Development (DEV), Test (TEST), and Production (PROD) systems linked by a common SAP Transport Management System route. 
 M1: Landscape Initialized 
 Your S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition system is live and connected to SAP. Your implementation journey has now begun. 
 This milestone is triggered when the first EarlyWatch Alert data is received from any non-production system in the track. It marks the moment the landscape becomes visible to SAP. No thresholds and no configuration are needed. The mere presence of this data confirms that provisioning is complete and the system is connected. 
 M2: Realize Phase Active 
 Your team has started configuring the system for your business needs. Build and testing activities are now underway. 
 Detected through usage of transaction SPRO (the SAP Customizing Implementation Guide) on a DEV or TEST system. SPRO is the central entry point for system configuration, so its usage is a reliable signal that the implementation team has begun tailoring the system to the customer's business processes. 
 M3: Pre-Cutover Preparation 
 Access roles and authorization profiles are being set up. Go-live preparation is underway. 
 Detected through usage of transaction PFCG (Role Maintenance) on a non-production system. Setting up authorization roles and user profiles is a critical pre-go-live activity. 
 M4: Cutover Initiated 
 Your team has initiated the cutover; configuration is being transported to your production system. Go-live is imminent. 
 Triggered when a significant transport wave is detected on the production system: at least 1,000 Workbench and Customizing transport objects imported in a single week. This threshold distinguishes genuine cutover deployments from routine maintenance imports and provides a high-confidence signal that go-live preparation is in its final stage. 
 M5: Go-Live Detected 
 A significant jump in active users on your production system confirms go-live. Your system is now in productive use. 
 SAP EarlyWatch Alert tracks weekly active user counts on the production system. When a significant and sustained spike in users is detected, the system is considered live. The detection automatically adapts to the size of each customer's landscape, so it works equally well for small and large deployments. It also accounts for special cases like system conversions and filters out technical-only activity to avoid false positives. 
 M6: Steady Usage State 
 Your system is in stable productive use with an active user base and regular updates. The status is reviewed continuously and may change. 
 Unlike M1 through M5, which are set once and remain, M6 is a living indicator. It is re-evaluated every week and can change between "Reached" (healthy) and "At Risk" based on two independent checks. 
 M6-1: Transport Activity Check. Were any transports imported into any system in the track within the last six months? If not, the system may no longer be actively maintained. This check runs independently of go-live status, so it can flag adoption stalls even before a customer has gone live. 
 M6-2: User Decline Detection. After go-live, the system continuously monitors whether the number of active users on the production system is declining significantly. A sustained drop in usage serves as an early signal for customer success teams to reach out and offer support. 
 Remark: Some milestones can be calculated based on the availability of connected Private Cloud systems. 

 Where to Find It 
 The milestone data is available in the Customer Insights Dashboard (CID) on SAP for Me, in the Onboarding tab: https://me.sap.com/reporting/customerinsightsdashboard/onboarding 
 If you are already using the Onboarding view for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition or SAP IBP, you will find the Private Cloud milestones right alongside them. Same dashboard, same experience, no additional setup: 

 When M6 turns red, it provides a specific, actionable signal: either maintenance activity has stopped or the productive user base is declining. Both are leading indicators of adoption challenges, and both are surfaced early enough for proactive engagement. 

 Conclusion 
 Adoption milestone tracking for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition transforms EarlyWatch Alert data, collected every week from every connected system, into structured, actionable adoption intelligence. By automatically identifying where each customer stands in their cloud journey and flagging early signs of risk, it enables the kind of proactive, data-driven engagement that complex cloud transformations demand. 
 Read more about how this helps you get the most out of your SAP investment: Proactive by Design: Introducing Adoption Milestone Tracking for S/4HANA Private Cloud - SAP Community

title: SAP RAP Question: Allowing Another User to Edit Drafts
author: ajay_mukundan2
text:
In RAP with draft handling (similar to the standard Manage Purchase Orders app), how can a draft that is currently owned by one user be made editable by another user? e.g. when the draft owner got ill / left the organization etc.... 
 By default, RAP draft instances are locked and owned by the user who created them. Is there a standard RAP mechanism, configuration, or extension pattern that allows another authorized user to take over, share, or continue editing an existing draft? Alternatively, how is this requirement handled in standard SAP Fiori apps such as Manage Purchase Orders ? 
 As per the ABAP RAP documentation, in RAP (ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model), draft handling offers two main modes: exclusive drafts and collaborative drafts. 

 Exclusive Draft Handling: Drafts are locked exclusively by the user who created them. Only the draft owner can modify, activate, or discard the draft. This means no other user can edit another user's drafts. 

 Collaborative Draft Handling: Multiple users, once authorized and invited with the "Share" draft action, can concurrently edit the same draft. 
 In the latter approach, its a real pain for End users to keep inviting other users. Is there an alternative to enable Draft-handling by multiple users like the way 'Manage Purchase Order' app does? 

 Any guidance, best practices, or examples would be appreciated.
